Author: Sharad Kumar Sharma
Bench: Sharad Kumar Sharma

S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  18.10.2023  C482 No. 2082 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Pawan Mishra, Advocate, for the applicant.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, Deputy Advocate General, for the State.

On reading of the FIR, as well as the statements recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, the facts,
which are revealed are, that the complainant and the present applicant were in a friendly relationship for last about more than 5 years and it was an admitted case of the complainant that she had travelled with him to Mussoorie; stayed in a Hotel called as 'Mall Palace', Mussoorie, and had established physical relationship with the present applicant.
For a momentary period, the relationship had broken and thereafter it was re- established when she had travelled to Nainital and stayed in 'Hotel Shalimar'.

It was complained of by the complainant that the aforesaid physical relationships were established under a false assurance of marriage, and hence she contends that there was an offence under Section 376 of IPC.
For establishing an offence under Section 376 of IPC
, the prime element, which is required to be established and considered, is that of a consent, as prescribed under Section 375 of IPC.

If a major female voluntarily travelled with a major male, to different places and stays in hotels and voluntarily establishes physical relations without any retaliation or registering of the complaint within the reasonable time frame, the consent is quite explicit in itself, which may not constitute as to be an offence under Section 376 of IPC.
Steps to serve the respondent would be taken by the applicant within a period of one week from today.
List as soon as the notice is served upon the respondent.
